overview: The two most clinically significant malaria species, differing sharply in severity, relapse potential, and red blood cell preference.
genZNote: P. falciparum shows up to every party uninvited (any RBC age, severe disease). P. vivax ghosts you and comes back later (hypnozoites, relapse).

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The malaria species responsible for the most severe and life-threatening form of malaria, with high mortality if untreated.
aspects.valueB: A malaria species causing a generally milder illness, notable for its ability to cause relapses months to years later.

aspects.label: Clinical Severity
aspects.valueA: Can cause severe malaria: cerebral malaria, severe anemia, acute kidney injury, and death.
aspects.valueB: Generally less severe, though can still cause significant morbidity; severe disease is less common.

aspects.label: Red Blood Cell Preference
aspects.valueA: Infects red blood cells of all ages, allowing very high parasitemia.
aspects.valueB: Infects only reticulocytes (young RBCs), limiting parasitemia.

aspects.label: Relapse Potential
aspects.valueA: No dormant liver stage — does not relapse (only recrudescence from incompletely treated blood-stage infection is possible).
aspects.valueB: Forms dormant hypnozoites in the liver, causing relapses months to years after the initial infection.

aspects.label: Blood Smear Appearance
aspects.valueA: Multiple ring forms per cell, banana-shaped gametocytes, no enlargement of infected RBCs.
aspects.valueB: Enlarged infected RBCs with Schüffner's dots, amoeboid trophozoites.

aspects.label: Geographic Distribution
aspects.valueA: Predominant in sub-Saharan Africa and other tropical regions.
aspects.valueB: Widely distributed, including South Asia and parts of Latin America; more common outside Africa.

aspects.label: Treatment Consideration
aspects.valueA: Requires prompt treatment (e.g. artemisinin-based combination therapy) due to risk of rapid deterioration.
aspects.valueB: Requires an additional course of primaquine or tafenoquine to eradicate liver hypnozoites and prevent relapse.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Infects any RBC age, no relapse, most severe disease.
aspects.valueB: Infects only reticulocytes, forms hypnozoites causing relapse.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Schüffner's dots + enlarged RBCs = P. vivax (or P. ovale). Banana-shaped gametocytes = P. falciparum.
